[1] ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models - arXiv
    URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629
    Published: 2022-10-06T00:00:00.000Z
    SUMMARY: The paper titled "ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models" explores a novel approach that integrates reasoning and action generation in large language models (LLMs). Traditionally, these two capabilities have been studied separately, but the authors propose a method where reasoning traces and task-specific actions are generated in an interleaved manner. This synergy allows reasoning to assist in creating, tracking, and updating action plans while actions enable the model to interact with external sources for additional information.

The ReAct approach is tested across various language understanding and decision-making tasks, showing significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods. For instance, in question answering (HotpotQA) and fact verification (Fever), ReAct mitigates common issues like hallucination and error propagation by utilizing a simple Wikipedia API, resulting in more interpretable task-solving trajectories. Additionally, in interactive decision-making benchmarks (ALFWorld and WebShop), ReAct achieves a 34% and 10% higher success rate compared to imitation and reinforcement learning methods, respectively, using only one or two in-context examples.

The paper emphasizes the enhanced human interpretability and trustworthiness of the model when reasoning and acting components are combined. For further details, the project site with code is available [here](https://react-lm.github.io).
